question: The Iron Age site named Tekwada is located in _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tekwada is an Iron Age site located in the state of **Maharashtra**, India.
 
• The site is known for its archaeological significance related to the **Iron Age**.
 
• Excavations at Tekwada have revealed artifacts such as pottery, tools, and remnants of ancient structures.
 
• It provides valuable insights into the lifestyle and technological advancements of ancient populations in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Age**:

 
 
• The Iron Age is a prehistoric period following the Bronze Age, marked by the widespread use of iron for tools and weapons.
 
• It began around 1200 BCE and lasted until the advent of written history in various regions.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Sites in Maharashtra**:
 
 
• Maharashtra is home to several significant archaeological sites, including Ajanta and Ellora Caves, known for their ancient rock-cut architecture and paintings.
 
• Other notable sites include the Karla and Bhaja Caves, which provide insights into early Buddhist architecture.
 
 
 
• **Pottery in Iron Age**:
 
 
• Pottery was a major artifact found at Iron Age sites, reflecting the technological and artistic capabilities of the era.
 
• Different types of pottery, such as black and red ware, have been discovered, indicating diverse cultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Excavations**:
 
 
• Excavations help in uncovering historical artifacts and structures, providing a window into ancient civilizations.
 
• They are crucial for understanding the development of human societies and their technological advancements.
